newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peru rebels will persist until comrades released.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels will persist until comrades released.

text.p: A spokesman for Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages in Peru said on Wednesday they would not stand down until all of their jailed comrades were freed.

"We do not understand the word surrender...we will continue until we win the freedom of our prisoners," international spokesman for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), Isaac Velasco, told a news conference in Madrid.
MRTA rebels seized the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima 21 days ago during a diplomatic reception, demanding the release of some 400 imprisoned colleagues from Peruvian jails.
The guerrillas have freed more than 430 of their original captives but have said they will not release any more until the Peruvian government starts negotiations.
Velasco said an improvement in conditions for their jailed comrades would not be enough to end the deadlock.
"We will not accept an improvement in conditions in the prisons," he said.
"We have all the time in the world, the question is whether the people in there can sustain this. The government must do everything necessary for a prompt exchange of prisoners."
He said the government should not turn its back on dialogue.
"Everything is negotiable. We know it's difficult but dialogue is essential," Velasco said.
Peru's President Alberto Fujimori said on Wednesday his government would not give in to blackmail from the guerrillas.
However, Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi later said the government would continue "unofficial dealings" with the rebels to find a peaceful end to the crisis.
Velasco, a political exile living in Germany since 1994, called on the international community to put pressure on Peru to find a solution.
"Other countries can exert political and economic pressure on Fujimori's regime to solve the problems that caused this armed assault," he said.
He added that although conditions were tense within the ambassador's residence, the hostages were being treated well.
"All the hostages are being treated in a humane manner, something which our prisoners are not experiencing in Peru's jails," he said.
